status: Disclosure only (DECISIONS A9, A13): the model capacity factors are NOT calibrated to DUKES. DUKES values read from the DESNZ xlsx in F1 (docs/dev/REFERENCE_STATISTICS_FOR_AUTHOR_REVIEW.md 3.4).
model_basis: Unweighted mean over the pack's representative weather sites of the per-period dispatch availability (capacity factor), 17,520 half-hour periods, before curtailment and before market dispatch; computed by scripts/vre_cf_disclosure.py for each dispatch weather method.

dukes.basis: DESNZ DUKES 2026 table 6.3, load factor on the standard basis (generation / average of beginning- and end-of-year capacity) [X]; actual generation after curtailment and constraint actions, whole GB fleet.
dukes.source: DESNZ, Digest of UK Energy Statistics 2026, table 6.3 'Load factors for renewable electricity generation' (xlsx, published 2026-07-30, accessed 2026-10-06)
dukes.not_used: The DUKES 'wind total' row is not used: its 2020 and 2021 standard-basis values disagree with the components (reference statistics 3.4).

reasons.text: ERA5 100 m wind speeds are not bias-corrected; uncorrected reanalysis overstates north-west European wind output (Staffell & Pfenninger 2016, Energy 114:1224-1239). The literature loss factors do not remove this bias (A9).

One free-stream single-turbine power curve per site (cut-in 3 m/s, rated 9.7 / 10.5 m/s), without power-curve smoothing over a farm; wake, availability and electrical losses are applied as literature factors only (A9).
The model CF is the available output before curtailment; DUKES load factors are actual generation after curtailment and constraint actions.
The model CF is an unweighted mean over a few representative sites, not the capacity-weighted GB fleet; site selection may favour good resource (not verified).

GBP1 weather is an ERA5 2020-2024 average climatology (finding P6-09), not one historical year; for solar it lowers the clearness index, raises the diffuse share and shrinks the plane-of-array gain (A13).
DUKES solar generation of small installations is estimated with a typical load factor (DUKES 6.2 note 8), so the solar comparison is less precise than wind.
VALUE 101 weather is synthetic teaching data; its capacity factors are not comparable with DUKES.
